title: Army opens premier test ranges to private industry for rapid innovation
key_claim: The Army is opening four stateside test ranges plus an international range in Morocco to private industry, with a public reservation portal and a dedicated concierge, and no prior government contract required to submit a request.
frame_summary: The Army is arguing that access to instrumented test environments, not money or contracts, is what has been keeping good equipment out of soldiers' hands, and that the fix is to run range booking like a commercial service.
verbatim_quote: In addition to standard testing, the Army will also host a special electromagnetic unreliability test event for private industry at Camp Grayling during the week of Sept. 13, 2026.
verbatim_list: A company with a good idea shouldn’t need a team of lawyers and a program of record just to prove their equipment works
Private industry does not need to have a prior U.S. government contract or existing federal relationship to submit a request.

title: EDA to coordinate ammunition qualification tests
date_evidence:
Latest news

30 March 2026

EDA to coordinate ammunition qualification tests
key_claim: A manufacturer supplying the same ammunition to several EU member states often has to repeat testing and approval in each country; the EUR 50 million Joint Ammunition Qualification programme aims to make a round tested once acceptable everywhere, starting with 155 mm.
frame_summary: EDA is arguing that Europe's ammunition shortfall is partly a paperwork geography problem, because the same physical round has to be re-proved country by country, and that mutual recognition of test results is therefore an industrial-capacity instrument.
verbatim_quote: The European Defence Agency (EDA) will coordinate the Joint Ammunition Qualification (JAQ) programme, funded with €50 million from the European Commission under the European Defence Industry Programme (EDIP).
verbatim_list: So far, a manufacturer supplying the same ammunition to several countries often has to repeat testing and approval processes in each country, in line with rules and procedures that may differ.
It will initially focus on 155 mm artillery ammunition, identified as a priority by Member States.
JAQ aims to introduce common procedures so that ammunition tested in one Member State would not need to be re-tested in other EU countries.

title: The Defense Ramp-up Reality Check: Scaling the US Defense industrial base to meet record demand
key_claim: A May 2026 survey of over 160 US defence suppliers found suppliers holding reserve capacity as insurance against sub-tier risk, and recommends mapping suppliers by qualification lead time and certification constraints rather than by procurement spend.
frame_summary: Oliver Wyman is arguing that the ramp is being held back less by absolute capacity than by mistrust and invisibility across tiers, so the practical lever is making constraints such as qualification lead time and certification legible rather than buying more factory floor.
verbatim_quote: As many small and specialized suppliers carry the highest risk, Primes and Tier 1s should map suppliers and processes by schedule criticality, substitutability, qualification lead time, and ramp risk — not only procurement dollars.
verbatim_list: In May 2026, we gathered detailed responses from over 160 companies, including original equipment manufacturers, Tier 1 suppliers, and sub-tier suppliers.
Critical suppliers should be able to communicate current rates, labor gaps, tooling limits, material lead times, quality blockers, certification constraints, and realistic recovery timelines.
notes: Survey-based Tier 2 source. Introduces qualification lead time and certification as first-class supply-chain constraints.
